review.reason: Candidate 34 passes as supplied. Hole 1 is a dry 225-yard par 3 with fairway bunkers short of the green and a playable approach; it offers a clear distance-control test to open the round. Hole 2 is a 553-yard par 5 with one substantial lake on the right of play and fairway bunkers on the opposite side. The broad corridor leaves a staged route, while favoring one side brings the other hazards into consideration. Hole 3 is a dry 413-yard double dogleg: the bends and fairway bunkers reward placement, and the tree clusters give the more direct line some consequence. The dry par 3, shoreline par 5 and bending par 4 create strong contrast. Recent rounds feature many water hazards, so limiting water to one hole adds freshness; the sequence and varied hole types distinguish this set. Safe tee options of 67/54/55 and usable landing corridors support fair difficulty. The simulated two-shot route on the par 5 indicates an aggressive possibility, not proof that the hole is effortless. No geometry edits are needed.
